bridge: Builds on P06 environments, L03 version history and S01 assets.
teaching:
Software depends on packages, build tools and release infrastructure. An inventory should identify exact versions and provenance, including transitive dependencies where relevant. A familiar package name does not establish that the downloaded artifact came from the intended publisher.

Keep secrets outside committed source and public build logs. Revoking a leaked credential is different from deleting its visible line; copies and history may remain. Use short-lived, least-privilege credentials where the platform supports them, and document rotation/recovery.

Supply-chain controls can include lockfiles, verified sources, isolated builds, review and artifact provenance. None makes dependency updates unnecessary. Triage an advisory by affected version, reachability, exploit prerequisites and available fix rather than upgrading blindly or dismissing every unused-looking function without evidence.
example:
Synthetic inventory
app -> parser-lib1.2 -> text-core3.0
Advisory: parser-lib versions below1.3 mishandle oversized records.
App accepts untrusted records through parser-lib.
Plan: reproduce with harmless fixture; update to fixed supported version;
verify normal/oversized cases; record lockfile and artifact source.
No real package names or model calls are involved.
explanation: The dependency is reachable from the app's input path, so the advisory is relevant under the fixture. A version comparison alone does not prove exploitability, but the observed call path strengthens the prioritisation. Record any temporary size limit and its residual risk.
exercise: Create an inventory and triage note for the supplied graph. Add a fictional leaked read/write deployment token in an old commit. State immediate containment and longer-term history/build-log actions without using a real token.
solution: Rotate/revoke the exposed token promptly, review access and replace it with least privilege. Remove exposed material from relevant history/logs through an approved process, recognising that prior copies may persist. Do not rely on a new commit deleting the line.
challenge: A build uses a lockfile but downloads a tool from an unpinned script URL. Explain the uncovered dependency and propose a verifiable release record covering source, tool version, inputs and output artifact.
challenge_solution: The build tool is part of the supply chain even if absent from application dependency files. Pin/verify its source and version, isolate credentials and record artifact provenance with repeatable checks.
